title.value: CAMAP: Artificial neural networks unveil the role of codon arrangement in modulating MHC-I peptides presentation
title.justification: The paper introduces CAMAP, which is an artificial neural network developed to study the role of codon arrangement in the presentation of MHC-I peptides.
title.quote: We developed an artificial neural network called Codon Arrangement MAP Predictor (CAMAP), predicting MAP presentation solely from mRNA sequences flanking the MAP-cod- ing codons (MCCs), while excluding the MCC per se.

analysis.description: This paper presents a study on the role of codon arrangement in modulating the presentation of MHC-I associated peptides (MAPs) using an artificial neural network named CAMAP. The research shows that codon usage near MAP coding regions significantly influences MAP biogenesis. CAMAP provides a new approach to predicting MAPs by focusing on mRNA sequences flanking MCCs (MAP-coding codons), allowing for improved prediction accuracy, which can be crucial for designing vaccines and immunotherapy treatments. The paper also validates CAMAP predictions across different datasets and species, showing its wide applicability.

type.justification: The work involves the development and validation of an artificial neural network model using experimental datasets to predict and explain the role of codon arrangement in MHC-I peptide presentation.
type.quote: We show on several datasets that the integration of CAMAP scores with other known factors involved in MAP presentation (i.e. MAP ligand score and mRNA expression) significantly improves MAP prediction accuracy, and further validate CAMAP learned features using an in-vitro assay.

name.justification: The research primarily uses computational methods to study biological processes, particularly the role of mRNA codon arrangement in antigen presentation.
name.quote: This is a PLOS Computational Biology Methods paper.

name.justification: The study involves bioinformatics analysis to understand the impact of codon arrangement on MAP prediction accuracy.
name.quote: Our analyses of large datasets using artificial neural networks and other bioinformatics approaches provide compelling evidence that codon usage regulates MAP biogenesis via both short- and long-range effects.
